# Collision Matrix 3D **Seven lanes of head-on collisions, distributed in a 3×3 grid of depth — the SAME density-vs-bounce-timing law as the 2D matrix, now visibly receding into the z axis.** Seven pairs of Dim-6 bodies (same voxel size, same capacity) launch head-on along X. Mass is swept on a log (powers-of-2) scale from 1 to capacity, giving density ρ ≈ 0.0002 … 1.0. The 2D collision-matrix arranges these lanes in a single column; this version distributes them in rows (Y) and columns (Z) so the perspective orbit camera reveals TRUE DEPTH — bodies at different Z recede convincingly, not just stack vertically. Engine bench C5 (z-axis bounce ≡ x-axis bounce) means this 3D distribution is architecturally free — no new engine behavior, only a different placement of the SAME physics. *New to FRQTL? Start with **Hello, FRQTL** (`getting-started-hello-frqtl`) for the `caps.frqtl` setup-module + declarative-canvas basics this notebook assumes.* The scene — the collision-matrix-3d scene's sketch file, verbatim: seven mass-swept lanes distributed in Y and Z — as editable user code. Its first statement creates the 3D world (`exp.createScene`, a 700-cube), and it declares its own render intent (`exp.render({ shape: 'sphere', colorScheme: 'roygbiv' })`): /* Copyright 2023-2026 by Essam Abadir */ /** * SCENE — 3D Collisions Lab * * A sketch file: the WHOLE scene as one ES module, `export default function buildExperiment(exp)`. The 3D world, the * seven head-on lanes of equal-mass voxel pairs, their live knobs and the look are all here; the * lane density table (`collisionMatrixLanes`), the renderer and the engine are imports. * A row of egpt-frqtl's roster (rung collision-matrix-3d). * * Physics (zero new — bench C2, C3, C5, SU1): each lane fires two equal bodies at each other at * speed_prob 1 along x; a lane's density (mass / capacity) sets how hard the bodies are — rigid * bodies bounce cleanly, soft ones press into each other before parting. The lanes sit on a 3x3 * y/z grid, so the same contact happens at seven depths: collision is identical on any axis * (2D ≡ 3D). The same engine that makes light makes mechanics — no second physics. * * Order (it seeds the run): world → collisions on → the voxel layer → * per lane, body A then body B (engine-built, capacity read back once) → seat every body. */ import { CameraControls, FrqtlControlOverlay, FrqtlControlsPanel } from '@descix/frqtl-web/parts'; import * as ControlRegistry from '@descix/frqtl-web/shim/controls/registry.js'; import { collisionMatrixLanes } from '@descix/frqtl-web/objects/setup/_collisionMatrixLanes.js'; export const parts = {}; export default function buildExperiment(exp) { var W = 700, H = 700, D = 700; // THE WORLD this scene states (its co-init call below) var LEVEL = 6; // the voxel layer: 64 px bodies, capacity 4096 // ── WORLD — a 3D scene + universe W×H×D, fundamental layer 0, λ multiplier 1 ── exp.createScene(W, H, D, { dimension: 0, wavelengthScale: 1 }); exp.declare(parts); var u = exp.universe; u.withInterQuantumCollisions = true; u.addDimension(LEVEL); exp.runner.setRateLimits({ tpsLimit: 240 }); // pacing only: wall-clock, never the ticks var lanesTable = collisionMatrixLanes; // the ONE lane density table (imported) var voxel = Math.pow(2, LEVEL), half = voxel / 2; var midX = Math.floor(W * 0.5); var ax0 = midX - Math.floor(1.5 * voxel); // body A, left of centre var bx0 = midX + Math.floor(1.5 * voxel); // body B, right of centre var N = lanesTable.LANE_DENSITIES.length; // 7 lanes var spacing = Math.round(H / 4); var laneYs = [], laneZs = []; for (var k = 0; k < N; k++) { laneYs.push(Math.round(H / 2 + (Math.floor(k / 3) - 1) * spacing)); // rows 0,0,0,1,1,1,2 laneZs.push(((k % 3) - 1) * spacing); // cols 0,1,2,… } // The live knobs: an offset (the bodies miss by that much) and an angle (vy against vx). var offsetPx = 0, angleVy = 0; function seat(qid, cx, cy, cz, dirX, mass) { u.setFrameProperty(qid, 'x', cx); u.setFrameProperty(qid, 'y', cy + dirX * offsetPx); u.setFrameProperty(qid, 'z', cz); u.setFrameProperty(qid, 'vx', dirX); u.setFrameProperty(qid, 'vy', -dirX * angleVy); u.setFrameProperty(qid, 'vz', 0); u.setFrameProperty(qid, 'mass', mass); u.setFrameProperty(qid, 'speed_prob', 1.0); } // ── THE BODIES — A then B per lane; the capacity is read back from the engine, never assumed ── var built = [], capacity = null; for (var i = 0; i < N; i++) { var a = u.makeLeafFrame(ax0 - half, laneYs[i] - half, LEVEL, null, 1, 0, true, 0, null); u.injectFrame(a); var aQid = u.getFrameQuantumId(a); var b = u.makeLeafFrame(bx0 - half, laneYs[i] - half, LEVEL, null, -1, 0, true, 0, null); u.injectFrame(b); var bQid = u.getFrameQuantumId(b); if (capacity === null) { capacity = u.getFrameProperty(aQid, 'mass'); } built.push({ aQid: aQid, bQid: bQid }); } var masses = lanesTable.laneMassesForCapacity(capacity); var lanes = built.map(function (q, i) { return { aQid: q.aQid, bQid: q.bQid, mass: masses[i], laneY: laneYs[i], laneZ: laneZs[i] }; }); function reseatAll() { lanes.forEach(function (l) { seat(l.aQid, ax0, l.laneY, l.laneZ, 1, l.mass); seat(l.bQid, bx0, l.laneY, l.laneZ, -1, l.mass); }); } reseatAll(); // ── THE LOOK — lit spheres, coloured by fullness (sparse red → dense violet) ── exp.render({ shape: 'sphere', colorScheme: 'roygbiv' }); // ── THE KNOBS (on the canvas) + MOVE/LOOK pads ── var registry = ControlRegistry.makeControlRegistry(); registry.registerControls('collision-matrix-3d', [ { kind: 'scalar', id: 'offset', label: 'offset', min: 0, max: 48, step: 4, value: 0, fmt: function (v) { return String(v); }, onChange: function (v) { offsetPx = v; reseatAll(); }, place: { x: 0.02, y: 0.03 } }, { kind: 'scalar', id: 'angle', label: 'angle', min: 0, max: 1, step: 0.1, value: 0, fmt: function (v) { return v.toFixed(1); }, onChange: function (v) { angleVy = v; reseatAll(); }, place: { x: 0.02, y: 0.12 } } ]); // Chrome (a page only): expose the knobs to a host frame, and mount the overlay through the // runner's ONE door (runner.controlHost) — before a canvas is mounted (a notebook pane) there is // none, so the knobs stay in the exposed registry only. FrqtlControlsPanel.exposeRegistry(registry, { runner: exp.runner }); if (exp.runner.controlHost) { FrqtlControlOverlay.mount(exp.runner, { registry: registry, name: 'collision-matrix-3d' }); } if (typeof document !== 'undefined') { if (exp.runner.controlHost) { CameraControls.attach(exp.runner, exp.runner.controlHost); } } } Declare a `shape="recipe"` canvas that runs it: `setup=""` + `seed` — no `stage`, because the scene states its own world. `render3d="true"` boots the three.js display the scene's `createScene` needs. Click **Run** (or **Run All**): ## What you are seeing Seven pairs of bodies, drawn as lit spheres and arranged in a 3×3 grid facing the camera, collide head-on. All seven lanes make first contact together (tick 64 at seed 42); how long a lane stays merged before separating varies NON-monotonically with its density under the per-tick occupancy-ceiling law — the same law the 2D collision-matrix demonstrates, now visible with true perspective depth: spheres further back in Z genuinely recede, rather than merely stacking on a flat plane. **Compare to the 2D version** (`collision-matrix`): identical physics, identical lane masses — the ONLY difference is the render intent (`render3d`) and the lane distribution (Y×Z grid instead of a single Y column), both of which the scene encodes; this notebook cell holds that same scene. The simulation runs live in your browser on the compiled FRQTL (WASM) engine.
